posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
Licco said:

Click to expand...
There is a plugin, I believe, by PheonixKageDesu that allows you to show gifs similar to the way you would use a show picture command. I don't have a link handy, but I am sure googling "RPG Maker MV plugin show gif" or similar keywords will turn up what you are looking for.
That said, for simple animations such as throbbers, you'd want to use a spritesheet.
The 3 frame walk cycle sprite sheet won't work because it ping-pongs, so the throbber will look like it plays clockwise and then counter-clockwise.
You can use a 4 frame animation by putting each frame in each row of a sprite sheet, then use a move route:
Turn down
Wait x frames (x determines the speed at which it throbs)
turn left
Wait x
Turn right
Wait x
Turn up
Wait x
Tick the repeat motions box.
You can also extend this to even more frames by making another index on the sprite sheet (like another character that you'd see on the large npc sprite sheets).
So for the first 4 frames you do exactly as I said about, down, left, right, up with waits in between.
Next you'd use the change actor picture (I forget what the editor calls the command, but something like that)
Select the second index with the next 4 frames, and repeat the commands.
I personally find it easier to organize frames in a snaking up-down pattern. So like: down, left, right, up, up, right, left, down, etc. This means you don't have to change the actor direction when you also change the actor picture.
